en: One: Xianfeng Beijing
zh: 第一章　先锋北京

en: The invitation for the now historic 1989 “no U-turn” exhibit in Beijing at the National Art Museum of China presents a translingual puzzle.
The Chinese text at the top reads
(Chinese modern art exhibit). The English text at the bottom,
, anticipates a foreign audience. It also introduces a discrepancy that reveals the problem of translation when understood as a process of producing linguistic equivalencies.

What do we make of “modern” in Chinese versus “avant-garde” in English? Or of the French “avant-garde,” coined in the nineteenth century, in later Chinese and English contexts? Curator Gao Minglu explains that while
(modern) in 1980s China signified newness, he and the editor of the exhibit catalogue agreed that “ ‘avant-garde’ made more sense than ‘modern’ as a translation of the original Chinese title.”
Modern in English seemed outdated, suggesting even a period style. Avant-garde sounded cutting-edge. Gao notes that Chinese artists and critics first began using
(literally, forward guard) and
(literally, advance front) toward the end of the 1980s. It was only after 1989 that they gradually replaced “modern” as descriptors for contemporary art practice.
zh: 1989年那场如今已载入史册的北京中国美术馆“禁止掉头”展览，其邀请函呈现出一个跨语言的谜题。
上方的中文写着“中国现代艺术展”。下方的英文“China/Avant-Garde”则预示着一个外国观众群体。它还引入了一处差异，揭示出把翻译理解为生产语言对等物之过程时的问题。
中文的“现代”与英文的“前卫”该如何理解？19世纪创造的法文“avant-garde”，在后来中文与英文语境中又意味着什么？策展人高名潞解释说，在20世纪80年代的中国，“现代”（xiandai）意味着新，但他和展览图录编辑一致认为，“用‘前卫’来翻译原中文标题比用‘现代’更说得通”。
英文的“modern”显得过时，甚至暗示一种时期风格；前卫听起来则很前沿。高名潞指出，中国艺术家和批评家直到20世纪80年代末才开始使用“前卫”（qianwei，原文释为“前方卫队”）和“先锋”（xianfeng，原文释为“前进的锋线”）。也是在1989年之后，它们才逐渐取代“现代”，成为当代艺术实践的描述词。

en: As Chinese art circulated under the label xianfeng/avant-garde in the 1990s, I found myself struck, at street level, by a Chinese context for the term that diverged from its cultural career in the West. I regularly slid money through a subway ticket window under a brass plaque engraved with the characters

(vanguard worker designation), a distinction awarded to units demonstrating an exemplary socialist work ethic. I noticed the honorary title on red and gold placards displayed in the front windows of public buses. I recognized its cognate of

(young pioneers) on elementary school banners and in the nationalist children’s anthem whose lyrics impel young heirs of the Communist mantel to courageously advance toward victory. I noticed it in advertisements for electronics equipment, articles on home decorating, and public injunctions for Beijing to succeed in its bid for the Olympics, as well as on the cover of new art journals like
(Avant-garde today).
It was a term still in flux, with a past that lived on in present juxtaposition with new meanings.
zh: 20世纪90年代，中国艺术以先锋/前卫（xianfeng/avant-garde）的标签流通时，我在街头层面被该词的中国语境所触动，它与这个词在西方经历的文化历程并不相同。我经常从地铁售票窗口递钱，窗口上方钉着一块铜牌，刻着“工人先锋号”（gongren xianfeng hao）——一种授予展现模范社会主义劳动伦理的单位的称号。我在公共汽车前窗的红金色标牌上注意到这一荣誉称号。我认出它的同源词“少年先锋队”（shaonian xianfeng dui）出现在小学横幅上，也出现在那首民族主义儿童歌曲里，歌词激励共产主义的年轻继承者勇敢向胜利前进。我在电子产品广告中注意到它，在关于家居装饰的文章中，在北京申奥成功的公共号召中，以及《今日先锋》这类新艺术杂志的封面上看到它。
这是一个仍在变动的词，它的过去与新的含义并置，活在当下。

en: As a descriptor for the field I entered, xianfeng signifies the historical, political vanguard of Beijing as national capital

the forms of artistic activity it has fostered over time. It connotes revolutionary militarism and cultural cosmopolitanism. Only by assembling the translingual fragments of avant-garde/qianwei/xianfeng can we make sense of their cultural encounter in the context of Chinese contemporary art. Take for example the painting of a young woman in Red Guard uniform on the cover of a book titled

children: The Condition of Chinese Avant-Garde Art

en: (figure 1.01). Qi Zhilong’s

references a Maoist history of vanguardism, yet is infused with the soft come-hither glow of contemporary commodity culture. It appeals to Western desires for a Chinese avant-garde as political fetish that ventriloquizes liberal freedom of expression. It represents a Chinese break from the collectivized past of Maoist modernity even while remaining influenced by its revolutionary aesthetics. It also represents the persistence of gender politics in the confluence of avant-garde ideologies.
zh: 作为对我所进入领域的描述，xianfeng 既意味着北京作为国家首都的历史性政治先锋，也意味着它长期培育的艺术活动形式。它包含着革命尚武精神与文化世界主义。只有把 avant-garde、qianwei、xianfeng 这些跨语言碎片组装起来，我们才能理解它们在中国当代艺术语境中的文化相遇。以一本题为《中国前卫艺术状况》的书封面为例（图1.01），画中是一位穿红卫兵制服的年轻女子。祁志龙的《中国姑娘》指涉毛泽东主义的先锋历史，却又注入当代商品文化那种柔软诱人的光晕。它迎合西方对中国前卫的欲望——把中国前卫当作一种政治恋物，替西方代言自由表达。它代表中国对毛泽东主义现代性集体化过去的断裂，同时又仍受其革命美学影响。它也代表着性别政治在前卫意识形态汇流中的持续存在。

en: This chapter examines the remaking of Beijing first through an overview of cultural policy in relation to the capital city, and of avant-garde genealogies.

It then portrays this remaking through a montage of ethnographic fragments organized around key art institutions—academy, palace, village, and museum—as they shift from sites of revolutionary nationalism to culture industry formation. Montage as method underlies the composition of this book, which assembles an account of cultural transition from closely observed ethnographic fragments and builds its argument across chapters. It is an assemblage whose theory of knowledge arises from dialectical contrasts between colliding myths of progress and modernity. Its compositional aesthetics reflect those of the artists I focus on, whose works often represent “dialectics at a standstill.”

Bringing gender to the analysis heightens awareness of the relationship between avant-gardism and nationalism, and thus the need to deconstruct the avant-garde myth of originality as a repressive and colonizing technology whose professed faith in renewal and innovation masks its power plays.
zh: 本章首先概述与首都相关的文化政策及前卫谱系，以考察北京的再造。

随后，本章通过围绕关键艺术机构——学院、宫、村和博物馆——组织的一组民族志碎片蒙太奇，描绘这种再造，观察它们如何从革命民族主义的场所转变为文化产业的形成之地。蒙太奇作为一种方法，是本书构成的底层逻辑：它从细致观察的民族志碎片中组装出一部文化转型叙述，并跨章节构建论证。这是一个拼装体，其知识理论产生于相互碰撞的进步神话与现代性神话之间的辩证对照。它的构成美学也映照我所聚焦的艺术家的美学，他们的作品常常表现“停顿中的辩证法”。
把性别带入分析，会提高对前卫主义与民族主义之关系的自觉，也因此更需解构关于原创性的前卫神话——一种压制性的殖民化技术，它对革新与创新的公开信仰掩盖着权力游戏。

en: Cultural Capital
zh: 文化资本

en: The artists I interviewed lived in locations scattered throughout Beijing, a megacity at the turn of the millennium of more than 10 million people. The logistics of my research involved spending significant time on the subway, on buses, in cabs, or on carts attached to the back of three-wheeled motorcycles. In a Shijingshan District classroom, a college art teacher painted a wall-sized canvas crowded with popular figures ranging from politicians to movie stars, in a style influenced by propaganda posters and folk art. In the semirural Western Hills, a painter-turned-video artist from Anhui vented about local and global cultural hierarchies in a rudimentary brick dwelling rented from a farmer. In a Chongwen District high-rise, a painter-turned-performance artist living in a concrete-box apartment on the tenth floor took photos from her window of the construction site next door. In Songzhuang artist village, a cluster of studios built on farmland in Tongzhou District, the “political pop” painter whose massive compound I visited with a group of curators wasn’t home. Instead, a hired apprentice from the countryside worked away on one of his paintings that fetched record prices on the international market.
zh: 我访谈的艺术家住在北京各处。世纪之交的北京是一座拥有逾千万人口的特大城市。我的研究后勤意味着要在地铁、公共汽车、出租车或三轮摩托车后挂的板车上花费大量时间。在石景山区的一间教室里，一位大学美术教师画了一幅满墙大小的油画，画中挤满从政治家到电影明星的流行人物，风格受宣传画和民间艺术影响。在西山半乡村地区，一位来自安徽、从画家转行的录像艺术家在向农民租来的简陋砖房里，发泄对地方与全球文化等级的不满。在崇文区一栋高层建筑里，一位从画家转行的行为艺术家住在十楼的混凝土火柴盒公寓中，从窗口拍摄隔壁工地。在宋庄艺术家村——通州区农田上建起的一片画室群——我随一群策展人去了那位“政治波普”画家的巨大院落，但他不在家。一个从乡下雇来的学徒正替他画一幅在国际市场上创下纪录价格的画。

en: In spite of their differences, these artists routinely reiterated Beijing’s status as China’s “cultural center” (

), although their counterparts in the provinces often asserted the freedom of being “far from the emperor’s eye.” This belief in Beijing’s prominence persisted through the 1990s in spite of the fact that contemporary art exhibits in the capital were shut down with greater regularity than in other cities with burgeoning art scenes like Shanghai or Chengdu. The infamous reputation of the Beijing Ministry of Culture led to jokes about how censorship of an exhibit guaranteed foreign attention. When I asked artists, especially those without Beijing residence permits, work units, or familial connections, why they wanted to live there, some mentioned the large number of universities, including the Central Academy of Fine Arts, a historical sense of Beijing as imperial seat of culture, or even the creative tension of official opposition. Others responded along the lines of “because I can meet people like you,” meaning a foreigner. Beijing’s embassy districts and foreign-owned galleries catering to overseas buyers led to the development of a patronage system that attracted curators and art brokers from abroad. This magnetism eventually became a resource for the state’s remaking of Beijing.
zh: 尽管有种种差异，这些艺术家仍经常重申北京作为中国“文化中心”（wenhua zhongxin）的地位，尽管外省的同行常说“天高皇帝远”的自由。这种对北京重要性的信念在整个20世纪90年代持续存在，尽管首都的当代艺术展比上海或成都等艺术场景蓬勃发展的城市更频繁地被关闭。设在北京的文化部声名狼藉，以致人们开玩笑说，一个展览只要被查禁，就保证能引起外国关注。当我问艺术家——尤其是那些没有北京户口、单位或家庭关系的人——为什么想住在这里时，有人提到这里大学众多，包括中央美术学院；有人提到北京作为帝国文化中心的历史感；还有人提到官方反对所带来的创造性张力。其他人的回答则是“因为我能遇到像你这样的人”，意思是外国人。北京的使馆区和面向海外买家的外资画廊促成了一个赞助网络，吸引来自国外的策展人和艺术经纪人。这种吸引力最终成为国家再造北京的一项资源。

en: After the controversial closures of the
exhibit in 1989, followed by the events of June 4, the national Ministry of Culture initially turned its sights toward the south. The first China Art Exposition (

), the nation’s largest showcase of contemporary art, was launched in 1993 in Guangzhou’s Chinese Import-Export Commodities Trade Center. This linkage between art and commerce occurred one year after Deng Xiaoping’s highly publicized tour of the south. During his visit to the special economic zones of Guangzhou and Shenzhen, he praised their commercial successes and advocated market reform as the way for China to overcome its recent domestic turmoil and open connections with the world through trade.
zh: 1989年中国现代艺术展引发争议地关闭，随后又发生6月4日事件，国家文化部最初把目光转向南方。1993年，全国最大的当代艺术展示会——第一届中国艺术博览会（Zhongguo yishu bolanhui）——在广州的中国进出口商品交易中心推出。艺术与商业的这种联结，发生在邓小平高调南巡一年之后。在访问广州和深圳经济特区期间，邓小平称赞其商业成就，主张把市场改革作为中国克服国内动荡、通过贸易与世界连接的道路。

en: In 1995, organizers moved the China Art Expo to Beijing, claiming its location in Guangzhou had not garnered sufficient international attention. In the early 2000s, the weeklong art exposition continued to be held every summer in Beijing’s International Exhibition Center. Rows of numbered booths, rented by artists, galleries, art schools, publishing houses, antique dealers, and companies promoting art and culture, filled two cavernous halls. Many artists welcomed the Expo, in spite of its Ministry of Culture sponsorship, as an alternative to official exhibition spaces. After an initial period of enthusiasm, some dismissively likened the Expo to a hodgepodge marketplace, a maze of street stall

(independent entrepreneurs), with no distinction between good and bad. The most disparaging had begun showing their work in Beijing’s foreign-run galleries. Their desire for the distinction of market valuation ran counter to one of the original rationales for the Expo, a commercial twist on the socialist goal of “serving the people”: that offering art at affordable prices would combat elitism and make the nation’s art accessible to the general public.
zh: 1995年，组织者把中国艺术博览会移到北京，称其广州选址未能获得足够的国际关注。21世纪初，为期一周的艺术博览会仍每年夏天在北京国际展览中心举行。艺术家、画廊、美术学校、出版社、古董商以及推广艺术与文化的公司租下成排编号展位，填满两个巨大展厅。尽管博览会由文化部主办，许多艺术家仍把它当作官方展览空间之外的替代选择而欢迎它。最初的热情过后，一些人轻蔑地把博览会比作大杂烩市场，一个由街边摊位个体户（getihu）组成的迷宫，好坏不分。最不屑一顾的人已开始在北京外资画廊展出作品。他们对市场估值区隔的渴望，与博览会最初的理据之一相抵触——那是对社会主义“为人民服务”目标的商业式改写：以可负担的价格提供艺术，将对抗精英主义，使全国艺术为普通公众所接近。

en: The move of the Expo also represented a symbolic struggle between north and south. After Guangzhou proved that promoting cultural festivals and programs was good for business, Beijing adopted the model. Jing Wang notes, “The recent hype about Beijing’s capital impact (

) was the result of an intensifying image race orchestrated and monitored closely by the Department of the Strategies of Cultural Development in Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Beijing. As Shanghai and Guangzhou shifted their emphasis of urban planning from industrial to cultural economy, Beijing followed suit.”
In 1996, Beijing’s Municipal Political Consultative Committee articulated a new development strategy, “founding the capital through culture” (

They highlighted Beijing’s historical heritage as a reserve of cultural capital that financial or commercial cities like Shanghai and Guangzhou could never attain. The city government soon began investing in the large-scale construction of new cultural institutions, a trend that accelerated after Beijing won the bid in 2001 for the 2008 Olympics.
zh: 博览会的迁移也代表着南北之间的象征性斗争。在广州证明推广文化节庆和项目有利于商业之后，北京采用了这一模式。王瑾指出：“近来关于北京‘首都效应’（shoudu xiao-ying）的炒作，是上海、广州和北京的文化发展战略部门精心编排并密切监控的一场形象竞赛不断加剧的结果。当上海和广州把城市规划重点从工业经济转向文化经济时，北京也紧随其后。”
1996年，北京市政协提出新的发展战略“文化立都”（wenhua lidu）。
他们强调北京的历史遗产是文化资本的储备，上海和广州这类金融或商业城市永远无法获得。市政府很快开始投资大规模建设新文化机构，这一趋势在北京2001年赢得2008年奥运会主办权后加速。

en: This race between Beijing and other Chinese cities to develop the “tertiary sector” of culture as proof of their global arrival represented a major shift in national spatial ideology. Maoist rhetoric celebrated the revolutionary qualities of the rural peasantry as a vanguard force in the communist nation’s progress. A post-Mao focus on urbanization made cities the new national object of desire and resignified rural people as backward or stuck in the past. State-disseminated discourse on

(quality) reinforced the idea that rural citizens, relative to their urban counterparts, most needed to raise their suzhi, even as official economic strategy led to widening material disparity between city and country.
This state redirection and investment in cities corresponded with a transformation from coercive to regulatory forms of governance.

For example, the Ministry of Culture, once viewed as a policing body, became the sponsor of the China Art Expo. In Jing Wang’s words, “The state’s rediscovery of culture as a site where new ruling technologies can be deployed and converted simultaneously into economic capital constitutes one of its most innovative strategies of statecraft since the founding of the People’s Republic.”
zh: 北京与其他中国城市之间这场发展文化“第三产业”、以证明其全球抵达的竞赛，代表着国家空间意识形态的重大转变。毛泽东主义修辞赞扬农村农民作为共产主义国家进步先锋力量的革命品质。后毛泽东时代对城市化的关注使城市成为新的国家欲望对象，并把农村人重新意指为落后或停滞在过去。国家传播的关于“素质”（suzhi）的话语强化了这一观念：与城市居民相比，农村公民最需要提高素质，即便官方经济战略导致城乡物质差距扩大。
国家对城市的重新定向和投资，与治理从强制性形式向规制性形式的转变相对应。
例如，文化部曾被视为管控机构，如今却成了中国艺术博览会的赞助者。用王瑾的话说：“国家重新发现文化，把它当作可以部署新的统治技术并同时转化为经济资本的场所，这是中华人民共和国成立以来最具创新的治国策略之一。”

en: Avant-Guard Genealogies
zh: 先锋谱系

en: Shi Xinning’s “

(figure 1.02) juxtaposes iconic symbols of the avant-garde of Western art and Chinese socialism. In a fictional encounter of “impossible reality”—an altered reproduction of an image taken at an official visit to an industrial exhibition by one of Mao Zedong’s official photographers (figure 1.03)—Shi depicts the chairman intently inspecting Marcel Duchamp’s

On the one hand, it references the Great Leap Forward, Mao’s campaign beginning in 1958 to transform the country through rapid industrialization, when exhibits of modern amenities became a staple of Cold War politics. A year after Mao’s tour of the biogas exhibition, evidence of China’s progress toward surpassing capitalist development within fifteen years, Khrushchev and Nixon hotly debated their nations’ technological superiority in a model American kitchen on display in Moscow.

Mao’s gaze turns a stove into a politic symbol of surpassing the enemy. On the other hand, Shi’s black-and-white painting references the avant-garde aesthetic of Marcel Duchamp, who promoted conceptual thought over visual pleasure. Duchamp’s idea of the readymade became the “antiart” move that secured his place of prominence in modern art history. Through a process of selection and alteration, he transformed ordinary manufactured objects into art.

, the urinal he signed R. Mutt and first exhibited in 1917, has come to serve as a critique of the museum’s institutional power to convey artistic value. (Shi’s image collision draws the humorous connection between urinal and biogas stove: of excrement powering modernity.) Preparations for a Duchamp retrospective exhibition were in fact contemporaneous with the photo of Mao’s exhibition visit; it eventually opened in 1963 at the Pasadena Museum of Art. Shi makes these two avant-garde visions proximal. His documentary style of painting, based on his training in socialist realism at Shenyang’s Lu Xun Academy of Fine Arts, mimics the way artists under Mao reworked historical paintings in response to political winds.

The resulting “impossible reality” imbricates the masculinist chess match of Cold War politics with that of Western modernist aesthetics. The readymade in Shi Xinning’s painting—the photograph he reproduces, the urinal he places in it—becomes a symbolic fetish animated by opposing versions of historicism and surpassing the other.
zh: 石心宁的《“杜尚回顾展”在中国》（图1.02）把西方艺术前卫与中国社会主义的标志性符号并置。在一次“不可能的现实”的虚构相遇中——毛泽东一位官方摄影师在参观工业展览时拍摄之图像的修改复制品（图1.03）——石心宁描绘主席专注地审视马塞尔·杜尚的《泉》。
一方面，它指涉大跃进，即毛泽东从1958年开始通过快速工业化改造国家的运动，当时现代生活设施的展览成为冷战政治的常见项目。毛泽东参观沼气利用展览——被视为中国正朝着十五年内赶超资本主义发展的目标前进的证据——一年之后，赫鲁晓夫与尼克松在莫斯科展出的美国样板厨房里，就各自国家的技术优越性展开激烈辩论。

毛泽东的凝视把一只炉子变成超越敌人的政治象征。另一方面，石心宁的黑白绘画指涉马塞尔·杜尚的前卫美学，他推崇概念思考高于视觉愉悦。杜尚的现成品观念成为“反艺术”举动，确立了他在现代艺术史上的显要地位。通过选择和改动，他把普通制成品变成艺术。他签署“R. Mutt”并于1917年首次展出的小便池《泉》，已成为对博物馆传达艺术价值之制度权力的批判。（石心宁的图像碰撞引出小便池与沼气炉之间的幽默联系：粪便驱动现代性。）杜尚回顾展的筹备，实际上与毛泽东参观展览的照片同时发生；展览最终于1963年在帕萨迪纳艺术博物馆开幕。石心宁使这两种前卫视野彼此邻近。他的纪实风格绘画基于在沈阳鲁迅美术学院接受的社会主义现实主义训练，模仿毛泽东时代艺术家根据政治风向修改历史画的方式。
由此产生的“不可能的现实”，把冷战政治的男性主义棋局与西方现代主义美学的棋局嵌合在一起。石心宁画中的现成品——他复制的照片、他放入照片中的小便池——成为一个象征性恋物，由相互对立的历史主义版本和超越对方之欲所激活。

en: In my conversations with artists, they often reflected ambivalently on what it meant to be called avant-garde. One artist had created an altar to Mao Zedong in the corner of his studio, an installation piece as he called it. He provided a revisionist history as he looped avant-garde back to the role of culture in Maoist thought. At the center of the installation was an old dresser mirror purchased at a junk market. The slogan “to serve the people,” now chipped and faded, had been painted in red at the top of the mirror. Cultural Revolution images of Mao stuck in its wooden border framed the face of whoever looked into the mirror. Other propaganda images and a pair of red candles were laid as offerings in front of the mirror. His memory of the Cultural Revolution contained scars—police had investigated him as a teenager for allegedly writing an anti-Mao slogan on a village wall—but he remained in awe of the pervasiveness of its aesthetic, the everyday influence of decorated mirrors like the one he’d found discarded. He disparaged the materialistic ethos that permeated the current era and the professionalized circuits of its so-called avant-garde: “In my view, if we’re talking about people who make so-called avant-garde art, I think Mao Zedong was the greatest avant-garde artist. He really was unmatched. Under his orchestration, the clothes that people wore, the soldiers’ uniforms, were all blue, everything was that kind of thing, with everyone standing together. For avant-garde artists to do this today, that would really be an amazing piece. My worship for Mao is as an artist.... He was really an artist not a politician. He really couldn’t be a politician.”
zh: 在与艺术家的交谈中，他们常常矛盾地反思被称为前卫意味着什么。一位艺术家在画室一角做了一座毛泽东祭坛，他称之为装置作品。他把前卫绕回毛泽东主义思想中文化的作用，提供了一种修正主义历史。装置中央是一面从旧货市场买来的旧梳妆镜。镜子上方用红漆写着“为人民服务”，如今已斑驳褪色。嵌在木边框里的毛泽东文革时期图像，框住任何照镜者的脸。镜前摆放着其他宣传图像和一对红烛作为供品。他对文革的记忆带有创伤——十几岁时，警方曾调查他，指称他在村墙上写了反毛标语——但他对这种美学无孔不入的力量仍心存敬畏，比如他捡到的那面被丢弃的装饰镜，仍在日常生活中发挥影响。他贬斥弥漫在当下时代的物质主义风气，以及所谓前卫的专业化圈子：“在我看来，如果谈所谓前卫艺术的创作者，我认为毛泽东是最伟大的前卫艺术家。他真是无人能及。在他的编排下，人们穿的衣服、士兵的军装都是蓝色的，一切都是那一套，所有人站在一起。今天的前卫艺术家若能做到这一点，那才会是惊人的作品。我对毛的崇拜是作为艺术家……他真的是艺术家，不是政治家。他真的当不了政治家。”

en: At a dinner party of exactly the kind of artists he disparaged, contradictions still came to the fore. They gathered in a painter’s renovated apartment, which had just been featured in an interior design magazine. After discussion about home decorating principles, the pros and cons of ikea’s influence in Beijing, and the travails involved in securing visas for travel to overseas exhibits, the conversation turned toward the position of intellectuals in Chinese society. A debate broke out about Lu Xun, the highly regarded twentieth-century writer, social critic, and proponent of the leftist woodblock movement, canonized by the Chinese Communist Party after his death in 1936. One artist commented that for all their recent material accumulation and aspiration to cultural refinement, they couldn’t come close to Lu Xun’s lifestyle. He’d been reading Lu Xun’s diaries and was struck by the resources he had. Converting Lu Xun’s reported income into modern currency, he claimed it would be tens of thousands of yuan a month. In his assessment, Lu Xun spent most of his free time buying things—books, paintings, antiques, even old courtyard homes. Others joked that Lu Xun had become such an acerbic social critic because every morning he would bargain with art and antique dealers on Liulichang Street. Angry at being cheated out of a good price, he would return home and use his pen to curse people. As they debated whether this information about Lu Xun made him a cultural connoisseur to emulate or a leisured and thus hypocritical social critic, I realized that this literary gossip was about trying to figure out, via a reevaluation of a symbol like Lu Xun, their place in the national order of things.
zh: 在他所贬斥的那类艺术家的饭局上，矛盾依然浮现。他们聚集在一位画家翻新的公寓里，这套公寓刚被一本室内设计杂志报道。讨论过家居装饰原则、宜家在北京影响的好坏，以及出国参展签证的种种麻烦之后，话题转向知识分子在中国社会中的位置。一场关于鲁迅的争论爆发了。这位20世纪作家、社会批评家和左翼木刻运动倡导者备受尊崇，1936年去世后被中国共产党奉为经典。一位艺术家评论说，尽管他们近来积累了物质财富、追求文化修养，却远远比不上鲁迅的生活方式。他一直在读鲁迅日记，对其拥有的资源感到震惊。把鲁迅记载的收入换算成现代货币，他声称每月可达数万元。按他的判断，鲁迅大部分空闲时间都在买东西——书、画、古董，甚至旧四合院。其他人开玩笑说，鲁迅之所以成为如此尖刻的社会批评家，是因为他每天早上都在琉璃厂街与书画商和古董商讨价还价。因被坑了价钱而愤怒，他回家后用笔骂人。当他们争论这些关于鲁迅的信息究竟使他成为值得效仿的文化鉴赏家，还是一个有闲因而虚伪的社会批评家时，我意识到，这些文学八卦其实是在通过重新评价鲁迅这样的象征，弄清自己在国家秩序中的位置。

en: The images that many of these artists produced are cultural signs that point in different directions, a characteristic that emerges from and interrupts a Communist past. Tani Barlow observes, “All signs in a Maoist culture regime would, by definition, always have two potential referents. In theory, all national forms pointed backward to the national (and thus feudal) past and simultaneously forward to the bright potential of socialism. The Maoist framing of culture institutionalized this instability.”

As Chinese contemporary artists wrangled with what it meant to be avant-garde, they continued to embrace the instability of the Maoist cultural sign, even as they worked in a space of encounter like that of Shi Xinning’s painting, where “avant-garde” sparks different chains of genealogical signification.
zh: 这些艺术家中的许多人创作的图像，是指向不同方向的文化符号；这一特征从共产主义过去中浮现，并打断那个过去。白露观察到：“在毛泽东主义文化体制中，按定义，所有符号总会有两个潜在的指涉对象。理论上，所有民族形式既向后指向民族的（因而也是封建的）过去，同时向前指向社会主义的光明潜能。毛泽东主义的文化框定使这种不稳定性制度化。”
当中国当代艺术家争论前卫意味着什么时，他们继续拥抱毛泽东主义文化符号的不稳定性，即使他们是在像石心宁绘画那样的相遇空间中工作——在那里，“前卫”激发不同的谱系意指链条。

en: The term’s French origins date to the nineteenth century, when it connoted a close association between culture and socialist politics. Baudelaire used it in the 1860s as a term of contempt for leftist writers. Renato Poggioli traces how, after the 1871 suppression of the Paris Commune, the term came to refer to a separate artistic movement. The avant-garde, in his description, maintained an autonomous but parallel existence with the political left. Its practitioners were bohemian iconoclasts devoted to innovation and futurity. Poggioli further argues that the avant-garde could only flourish in a liberal society: “Avant-garde art is by nature incapable of surviving not only the persecution but even the protection or the official patronage of a totalitarian state and a collective society, whereas the hostility of public opinion can be useful to it.”

It thus depends on, even if through opposition to, free-market liberalism. Peter Bürger further argues that the embrace of the avant-garde by the very establishment institutions it opposed led to its death. When museums absorbed avant-garde art into a system complicit with capitalism, they neutralized its critical function.
zh: 这个词的法国起源可追溯至19世纪，当时它意味着文化与社会主义政治的紧密关联。波德莱尔在19世纪60年代用它来蔑视左翼作家。雷纳托·波焦利追溯了1871年巴黎公社被镇压后，这个词如何转变为指涉一个独立的艺术运动。在他笔下，前卫与政治左派保持自主但平行的存在。其实践者是献身创新与未来的波西米亚式偶像破坏者。波焦利进一步论证，前卫只能在自由社会中繁荣：“前卫艺术在本质上不仅无法在极权国家和集体社会的迫害下生存，甚至无法在其保护或官方赞助下生存，而舆论的敌意却可能对它有益。”
因此，它依赖自由市场自由主义，哪怕是通过与之对立的方式。彼得·比尔格进一步论证，正是前卫所反对的建制机构对它的接纳导致了它的死亡。当博物馆把前卫艺术吸收进与资本主义同谋的体系，它们便中和了它的批判功能。

en: “Avant-garde” entered Chinese through neologisms produced by early-twentieth-century translations of French, Japanese, and Russian sources. Chinese intellectuals working under the conditions of semicolonialism produced an era of furious translingual practice, as they brought concepts from foreign sources to bear on their struggle for national sovereignty. Art and politics in this context could not be understood as separate, as Gao Minglu argues in his theorization of China’s “total modernity,” marking its cultural and historical difference from the autonomous conception of the avant-garde in the West.
zh: “Avant-garde”经由20世纪初从法文、日文和俄文来源翻译中产生的新词进入中文。在半殖民主义条件下工作的中国知识分子，经历了狂热的跨语言实践时代，他们引入外来概念，以服务于争取民族主权的斗争。在这种语境中，艺术与政治不能理解为彼此分离，正如高名潞在关于中国“总体现代性”的理论化中所论证的，中国与西方前卫的自主观念之间存在着文化和历史差异。

en: An early use of the term appears in Lin Wenzheng’s review of the first
, held in Nanjing in 1928. He praises the work by several artists as “the avant-garde [

] of modern China’s art world,” and advocates an art of the people, supported by public institutions, that will raise their spiritual consciousness and national sensibility to a level equivalent with European society.

In Japan, the term appeared in formations such as Sasaki Takamaru’s Avant-Garde Theater and Kurahara Korehito’s Alliance of Avant-Garde Artists. Chinese dramatist Tian Han met both during his 1927 visit to Tokyo, during which Sasaki warned him against the empty rhetoric of artistic autonomy.

Kurahara had recently returned from the Soviet Union and became the leading Marxist theoretician during the Japanese proletarian art movement of the late 1920s and early 1930s. The kanji they used for avant-garde traveled back to China as qianwei.
zh: 这个词的早期使用出现在林文铮对1928年在南京举办的首届首都美术展览会的评论中。他称赞几位艺术家的作品是“中国现代艺术界的前卫（qianfeng）”，并倡导一种由公共机构支持的人民艺术，以把他们的精神意识和民族感受力提升到与欧洲社会相当的水平。
在日本，这个词出现于佐佐木孝丸的《前卫剧场》和藏原惟人的“前卫艺术家同盟”等组合中。中国剧作家田汉1927年访问东京时见过两人，佐佐木警告他不要空谈艺术自主。
藏原惟人最近从苏联归来，成为20世纪20年代末和30年代初日本无产阶级艺术运动的主要马克思主义理论家。他们用于“avant-garde”的汉字传回中国，成为“前卫”。

en: Other versions emerged in usages by the Guomindang, as well as by critics like Lu Xun. In 1930, the Guomindang government promoted a nationalist literary movement to counter the rise of revolutionary literature. New journals such as
(Avant-garde weekly) and

(Avant-garde monthly) published patriotic stories featuring heroic battle scenes. Lu Xun attacked one of these writers for his comparison of Chinese nationalists fighting warlords with French colonists fighting native Arabs in the African desert, as a telling identification with imperial masters.
One year later, he published a commemorative issue of the underground magazine

(Vanguard or Frontline) mourning the Guomindang execution of five left-wing writers. Through his support of the 1930s woodcut movement, Lu Xun advocated an avant-garde aesthetic that publicly called for a collective political struggle. After the Communist defeat of the Guomindang in 1949, the party codified this association in its claim to be the vanguard (xianfeng) of the proletariat, a term that in 1989 would be resignified once again by Chinese art world participants, through and in relation to previous histories.
zh: 国民党以及鲁迅等批评家的用法中，也出现了其他版本。1930年，国民党政府推动一场民族主义文学运动，以对抗革命文学的兴起。《先锋周报》（Qianfeng zhoubao）和《先锋月刊》（Qianfeng yuebao）等新刊物发表描写英雄战斗场面的爱国故事。鲁迅抨击其中一位作家把与军阀作战的中国民族主义者比作在非洲沙漠中与土著阿拉伯人作战的法国殖民者，认为这暴露了其对帝国主子的认同。
一年后，他在地下刊物《前哨》（Qianshao，意为 Vanguard 或 Frontline）出版纪念专号，哀悼被国民党处决的五位左翼作家。通过支持20世纪30年代木刻运动，鲁迅倡导一种公开呼吁集体政治斗争的前卫美学。1949年共产党击败国民党后，党把这种联系编入其作为无产阶级先锋队（xianfeng）的主张；这个术语在1989年又被中国艺术界参与者通过并与先前历史相关联地再次重新意指。

en: In her critique of modernist art discourse, Rosalind Krauss argues that the notion of the avant-garde depends on a discourse of originality, even though “the actual practice of vanguard art tends to reveal that ‘originality’ is a working assumption that itself emerges from a ground of repetition and recurrence.”

Promoters of Western modernism as an advancing force produce the avant-garde doctrine of newness, in part, by casting artists from other parts of the world as belated and derivative, closing off a history of the Western canon as itself a series of borrowings.

The rise of artistic modernism coincided with a period of rapid decolonization when European powers established legal agreements such as the Berne Convention to protect their ownership of works developed in colonial contexts and through non-Western influences.

Modern intellectual property regimes define and protect innovation, granting individual creators rights vis-à-vis the nation-state. The repressions of avant-gardism are deeply linked to the development of the modern militant nation-state and ideologies of surpassing. Introducing gender into the picture makes the act of deconstruction even more imperative.
zh: 罗莎琳德·克劳斯在批判现代主义艺术话语时论证，前卫观念依赖原创性话语，尽管“前卫艺术的实际实践往往揭示出，‘原创性’本身是一个从重复与再现的土壤中浮现的工作假设”。
把西方现代主义作为进步力量加以推广的人，部分通过把世界其他地区的艺术家塑造成迟到的、派生的，来生产前卫的新颖教义，同时封闭西方正典自身作为一系列借鉴的历史。
艺术现代主义的兴起恰逢快速去殖民化时期，欧洲列强建立伯尔尼公约等法律协议，以保护它们对在殖民语境中、通过非西方影响发展出的作品的所有权。
现代知识产权制度界定并保护创新，赋予个体创作者相对于民族国家的权利。前卫主义的压制与现代战斗性民族国家和超越意识形态的发展深刻相连。把性别引入图景，使解构行动更加迫切。
